Shamshir

Origin
Persia
Period
c. 1500 to 1800
Blade
80 cm
Weight

Edge
Single
Grip
One-handed

Shamshir is the Persian word for a sword with a strongly curved, single-edged blade. It is the type that English speakers often call a scimitar.

The curve suits slashing cuts, especially from horseback. Blades were often made of crucible steel, which shows a watered pattern on the surface.
